01.actor: A maidservant of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's household and Rabbi
01.event: The maidservant immersed, came up, and a bone was found between her teeth.
01.turn: The bone meant the immersion may not have covered her whole body.
01.outcome: Rabbi required her to immerse again.
01.summary: A maidservant in Rabbi's household immersed herself. When she came up, a bone was found between her teeth. Rabbi made her immerse a second time.

02.actor: Rav Yosef and his student Abaye
02.event: Rav Yosef said he had never heard a halakha, and Abaye reminded him that he himself had taught it, citing Rami bar Abba and Rav Huna and the three lessons Rav Yosef drew from it.
02.turn: Abaye showed the teacher had forgotten his own teaching (the text explains he had been ill and forgot his learning).
02.outcome: Rav Yosef's response is not shown; the halakha is later ruled to follow it.
02.summary: Rav Yosef said he had never heard a certain halakha from his teachers. His student Abaye told him that he had taught it to them himself, and quoted the statement and the three lessons Rav Yosef drew from it. The text explains that Rav Yosef had been ill and had forgotten his learning.
02.missing: Rav Yosef's reaction to being reminded, and a clear ending.

03.event: Rav Pappa served drinks at his son Abba Mar's wedding and poured a cup for Rav Yitzhak, son of Rav Yehuda.
03.turn: Rav Yitzhak did not stand up for him.
03.summary: At his son Abba Mar's wedding, Rav Pappa went around serving drinks. When he poured a cup for Rav Yitzhak, son of Rav Yehuda, Rav Yitzhak did not stand up before him. Rav Pappa was angry.

04.actor: A man whose betrothed wife had died, and the sages Rav Nahman, Ulla, Avimei and Rav Hiyya bar Ami
04.event: A man whose betrothed had died came before sitting sages, who told him to bury her or pay her marriage contract.
04.turn: Rav Hiyya objected, citing a teaching that a husband does not inherit from a betrothed wife.
04.outcome: No outcome for the man is shown; the objection leads into a legal discussion.
04.summary: Several sages were sitting together when a man came whose betrothed had died. They told him to bury her or pay her marriage contract. Rav Hiyya objected in surprise and quoted a teaching that a husband does not inherit his betrothed wife.
04.missing: What the man actually did or how the case ended.

05.actor: Rav Yehezkel and his sons Rami and Rav Yehuda
05.event: Rav Yehezkel taught Rami a mishna, and his son Rav Yehuda objected that he should teach it differently, and they argued over the wording.
05.turn: Rav Yehezkel countered that Yehuda's version had the same problem in the second half, and Yehuda answered it.
05.outcome: Later Shmuel told Rav Yehuda not to speak to his father so bluntly, and taught how to correct a father respectfully.
05.summary: Rav Yehezkel taught his son Rami a mishna. His other son, Rav Yehuda, told him not to teach it that way and proposed a reversed wording. Their father answered that the same objection applied to the other half, and Yehuda explained the difference. Shmuel later told Yehuda he was speaking disrespectfully to his father and should correct him gently by quoting the verse.

07.event: Rav Hisda praised Rav Hamnuna to Rav Huna, who asked to meet him, and saw he wore no head cloth.
07.turn: Rav Hamnuna said he was unmarried.
07.outcome: Rav Huna turned his face away and told him not to come before him again until he married.
07.summary: Rav Hisda praised Rav Hamnuna to Rav Huna as a great man, and Rav Huna asked to see him. When Rav Hamnuna came, Rav Huna saw he wore no head cloth and asked why. Hamnuna said he was not married. Rav Huna turned his face away and said he should not see his face until he married.

08.actor: Pishon the camel driver and his wife
08.event: Beit Hillel cited the case of Pishon the camel driver, whose wife refused him in his absence.
08.turn: Beit Shammai said Pishon had mismanaged her property, so the Sages penalized him.
08.outcome: The Sages treated it as a special case and allowed the refusal.
08.summary: Beit Hillel pointed to Pishon the camel driver, whose wife annulled the marriage without his being present. Beit Shammai said he had not looked after her property properly, so the Sages dealt with him by a defective standard. The text only alludes to the incident as a precedent.
08.missing: The actual events of Pishon's case; it is only referred to inside a dispute.

09.actor: The sons of Rav Huna bar Avin
09.event: They bought a maidservant to be paid in copper coins, and gave a piece of silver as collateral because they had no money.
09.turn: The maidservant's price rose, and the sellers wanted to cancel the sale.
09.outcome: Rabbi Ami ruled there were no coins and no silver given, so there was no valid sale.
09.summary: The sons of Rav Huna bar Avin bought a maidservant, to be paid for in copper coins. They had no coins, so they left a piece of silver as collateral. Her price then went up, and they came before Rabbi Ami. He ruled that no coins had been paid and the collateral did not count, so there was no sale.

11.event: A lentil bread in Mar Shmuel's days was thrown to his dog.
11.turn: The dog would not eat it.
11.outcome: This is used as an objection to Rav's ruling; it is answered in the next segment (the bread was mixed grain).
11.summary: In Mar Shmuel's days there was a lentil bread that he threw to his dog, and even the dog would not eat it. It is cited as a challenge to a ruling that lentil bread may be used for an eiruv.
11.missing: Who baked it and why; the story is only an objection to a ruling.

12.event: She tried to invite her friend to come and be fed milk.
12.turn: Her imprecise pronunciation turned the words into a different phrase.
12.outcome: She actually told her friend 'may a lioness eat you'.
12.summary: A Galilean woman wanted to say to her friend, 'Come and I will feed you milk.' Because Galileans did not pronounce the guttural letters properly, what came out was 'My neighbor, may a lioness eat you.'

14.actor: Bar Shatya and the witnesses, with Rav Ashi
14.event: Bar Shatya, who was sometimes insane, sold property, and two witnesses said he was healthy when he sold it while two others said he was insane.
14.turn: The two conflicting testimonies cancelled each other out.
14.outcome: Rav Ashi ruled the land stays in Bar Shatya's possession.
14.summary: Bar Shatya, a man who sometimes went insane, sold land. Two witnesses came to say he was healthy at the time, and two others said he was insane. Rav Ashi ruled to set the two pairs against each other and leave the land with Bar Shatya.

15.actor: Rav Hisda, Rava, and Elijah or Yosef the demon
15.event: Seven teachings said on Shabbat morning before Rav Hisda in Sura were repeated before Rava in Pumbedita by the end of that Shabbat.
15.turn: Someone must have carried them, though the distance was too far to walk on Shabbat.
15.outcome: The Gemara suggests Elijah, then rejects the proof, saying it may have been Yosef the demon.
15.summary: Seven teachings were said on Shabbat morning before Rav Hisda in Sura and again toward the end of the same Shabbat before Rava in Pumbedita. The distance was too great to walk. Elijah might have carried them by leaping through the air, but it may equally have been Yosef the demon, who does not keep Shabbat.
15.missing: Who really carried them; the passage is cited as a proof and left open.

16.actor: The daughter-in-law of the house of Bar Elyashiv
16.event: She claimed her marriage contract from the orphans and was bringing them to court.
16.turn: The orphans told her it was demeaning that she go in house clothes, so she dressed in all her clothes.
16.outcome: Before Ravina, he ruled that the court appraises the clothes on a widow, so what she wore counted against her payment.
16.summary: A woman of the Bar Elyashiv family was claiming her marriage contract from the orphans and taking them to court. They told her it was demeaning to them that she appear in plain house clothes, so she put on all her clothes. When they came before Ravina, he ruled that the court appraises the clothes on a widow and counts them toward her payment.

17.event: Rava served drinks at his son's wedding and poured cups for sages.
17.turn: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna stood before him, but Rav Mari and Rav Pinehas did not.
17.outcome: Rava became angry and asked whether those who stood were sages and the others were not.
17.summary: At his son's wedding Rava served drinks. When he poured for Rav Pappa and Rav Huna they stood up before him, but Rav Mari and Rav Pinehas did not. Rava got angry and asked whether some of them were sages and some were not.

18.actor: King Yannai, Elazar ben Po'ira, Yehuda ben Gedidya and the Pharisee sages
18.event: After conquering sixty cities, Yannai held a feast for the sages, where Elazar ben Po'ira told him the Pharisees resented him.
18.turn: Yannai had them stand before his frontplate, Yehuda ben Gedidya told him to give up the priesthood, and the sages were expelled in anger.
18.outcome: Elazar urged killing them, and the sages were killed and the world was desolate of Torah until Shimon ben Shatah restored it.
18.summary: King Yannai returned from conquering sixty cities and held a feast for the sages. Elazar ben Po'ira told him the Pharisees resented him and suggested testing them with the frontplate. Yehuda ben Gedidya told Yannai to give up the priesthood, since a rumor said his mother had been a captive, and the sages were driven out in rage. Elazar then urged Yannai to crush them, and all the sages were killed until Shimon ben Shatah restored the Torah.

19.actor: Rabbi Ami, Rabbi Yirmeya and Rabbi Zerika
19.event: A question was put to Rabbi Ami about a slave who gave himself to an army and whether the master may take his value.
19.turn: Rabbi Yirmeya sent Rabbi Zerika to look and he found a baraita about a house seized by force; this was challenged as not comparable.
19.outcome: Rabbi Ami sent a message ruling that the master may take the value.
19.summary: Rabbi Ami was asked about a slave who gave himself over to an army and whom the master could not recover. Rabbi Yirmeya sent Rabbi Zerika to check his teachings, and he found a baraita permitting a man to take the value of a house seized by force. That was challenged, but Rabbi Ami finally sent word that the master may take the slave's value.
19.missing: It is mostly a legal inquiry with a few steps of action.

20.event: Rav walked in among the sheaves in a field and saw them waving in the wind.
20.turn: He spoke to them as if they were boasting.
20.outcome: He told them that doing business is better than farming them; Rava then adds a related saying.
20.summary: Rav went into a field among the sheaves and saw them swaying in the wind. He said to them that they could wave if they liked, but business is better than farming them. Rava then gave a related saying about the poor returns of land.
20.missing: No real turn or ending; it is a brief anecdote used to make a point.
